previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for uncontrolled type I diabetes with hyperglycemia and ketonuria, consistent with diabetic ketoacidosis, following a viral illness with high fevers and oral herpes. She had no anion gap and stable vital signs, with normal lipase ruling out acute pancreatitis. Her blood glucose improved with continuation of home insulin therapy. Fevers resolved without identified bacterial source, and flu testing was negative. Chronic abdominal pain was managed with transition to oral Dilaudid, and she tolerated oral intake. Per narcotics agreement, no hospital prescriptions were issued. She was discharged with stable glucose levels, instructions to continue home insulin, and follow-up with her primary care provider for pain and oral lesions.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ with insulin dependent diabetes, h/o chronic 
pancreatitis, and ? gastroparesis, who presents from home with 
malaise, abdominal pain, and was found to have hyperglycemia.

# HYPERGLYCEMIA: Patient is on an insulin regimen prescribed by 
the ___ as well as an insulin pump which she uses between 
meals that she obtained ""elsewhere."" Her sugars were critically 
high in the ED and per patient during the day prior to 
admission. She turned off and removed her insulin pump prior to 
admission. Hyperglycemia most likely secondary to a combination 
of infection and poor compliance with medication regimen. She 
was started on lantus 20 qHS which was titrated up to 30 units 
qHS as her ___ intake increased with improved glycemic control. 
___ followed the patient during her hospitalization and 
recommended that she discontinue use of her insulin pump. She 
was discharged back on her home insulin regimen.
.  
#. ABDOMINAL PAIN: There was initial concern for biliary 
obstruction given elevated transaminases and alk phos. RUQ 
ultrasound was performed, and though limited secondary to pt 
positioning showed a echogenic liver w/o acute process. Her LFTs 
trended down. Patient's symptoms were controlled with her home 
___ dilaudid regimen and antiemetics per her care plan (zofran, 
compazine). Her symptoms improved and on discharge she was 
tolerating a regular diabetic diet. 
.
Given her history of recent episodes of acute pancreatitis with 
elevated lipase and the plan of her outpatient providers to 
pursue an MRCP with secretin, attempts were made to arrange this 
with anesthesia while she was an inpatient. Ultimately the 
patient decided she did not want to stay for the study and would 
pursue it as an outpatient.

mixed bacterial flora c/w contamination. Per OMR, received first 
dose of cipro ___. Given had completed about 3 days of 
antibiotics, d/c-ed antibiotics.

# CHEST PAIN: Patient complained of chest pain on admission. 
Pleuritic in nature. Improved without intervention. EKG similar 
to priors.

INDICATION:  ___ female with right upper quadrant pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Right upper quadrant ultrasound.

FINDINGS:  This examination was limited due to difficulty with patient
positioning and breath-hold.  The liver is slightly echogenic.  No
intrahepatic bile duct dilation or focal lesion is detected.  The main portal
vein is patent, demonstrating proper hepatopetal flow.  The patient is status
post cholecystectomy.  No neighboring focal fluid collections are seen.  The
CBD was not visualized due to patient motion.  No ascites is present.

IMPRESSION:  
1. Limited study due to difficulty with patient positioning.  Otherwise, no
acute process seen.
2. Echogenic liver, reflecting fatty infiltration. More advanced disease such
as fibrosis cannot be excluded with this technique.
